input: tokens is a list of n integer token costs in [0,10000], with 0 <= n <= 1000; power is an integer in [0,10000]. Integer inputs are plain int values excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists and strings are ordinary str values, without subclasses or overloaded behavior. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The largest score attainable from initial score zero, using each token at most once: pay its cost from power to gain one score, or spend one existing score to gain its cost in power. Token order is freely chosen. Empty tokens returns 0.
mutation_aliasing: Only a fresh copied ordering is sorted. The scalar power parameter is rebound locally, and no input token or caller container is changed. No play order is returned. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: Power stays nonnegative and is at most initial power plus all token costs, at most 10010000. Score and its maximum are in [0,n]. Indices range from -1 through n; comparator differences are in [-10000,10000]. All arithmetic intermediates are exact safe integers.
complexity: After sorting, O(n+1) two-pointer work consumes a different token each iteration. Buy the cheapest available token when affordable; otherwise, when another purchase can remain possible, sell the most expensive available token and retain the best score seen. Python copied sorting adds O(n*log(n+1)+1) time and O(n+1) auxiliary space.
